requirement:
`habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index use the same renderer for
their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables. The renderer calculates column
widths and aligns the columns. Each caller supplies its state labels:
`habeas status` reports checked evidence states, while the book reports
recorded assessments under {cite}`requirements.index.state`. The CLI keeps
its checked labels: Valid, Missing, Determination false, FIXME, and Invalid.
Callers may select different definitions and supply kind-labeled name cells
so mdBook can link to detail pages.
rationale:
structural: The one structural obligation is in this clause: "`habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index use the same renderer for their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables". A reimplementation that gave each caller its own table formatter would show the same output but break the clause. The clause therefore binds both callers to a shared renderer and needs implementation evidence. The roots supply it.

- `src/markdown.rs#fn[render_evidence_table]` is the shared renderer. It computes the Definition and Evidence column widths from the rows and the header names. It pads each cell to align the columns and emits the header, separator and rows. The text requires the width calculation and alignment.
- `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]` is the `habeas status` caller. It builds `(name cell, evidence.state().label())` rows and passes them to `render_evidence_table`. Its name cells are kind-labelled and unlinked, e.g. `` `name` (kind) ``. It chooses which definitions to include through the glob, `all` and `verbose` filters.
- `src/index.rs#impl[DetailPlan]/fn[populate]` is the mdBook caller. It builds rows with a link-bearing, kind-labelled name cell, `[`name`](href) (kind)`. It takes labels from the recorded evidence state and calls the same `render_evidence_table`. This is the delegation the clause requires.

The remaining clauses specify observable behavior only.
- The CLI "keeps its checked labels: Valid, Missing, Determination false, FIXME, and Invalid".
- The book reports recorded assessments.
- Callers "may select different definitions and supply kind-labeled name cells".

The label strings come from `src/index.rs#impl[EvidenceState]/fn[label]`. That function returns the checked labels for the CLI states and the Recorded labels for the book states. Any other mapping that produced the same strings would satisfy the text, so no structural marker is needed for it. In any case, the three marked roots already reach it.

The subject's own roots cover every structural obligation, so no missing root exists. `requirements.index.state` is cited context for the book's labels and adds no structural obligation here.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.cli.shared_status_rendering`.

**Same renderer, column widths and alignment**
- `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_tables_align_each_column_to_its_widest_cell]` runs `habeas status` four ways: default, `--all`, with a selection, and `--all` with a selection. It asserts three things for each run:
  - Pipe positions are identical on every row.
  - Each column is exactly as wide as its widest cell, with single-space padding.
  - The separator row has `---` cells.
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` makes the same pipe-position and widest-cell assertions on the mdBook index table.
- The two tables match in format, so a divergent renderer would be caught. "Uses the same renderer" is also an implementation choice with no further observable obligation.

**Caller-supplied labels**
- The CLI labels are checked in two tests. `status_tables_align_each_column_to_its_widest_cell` checks the row states Valid, Missing, Determination false and Invalid. `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]` checks FIXME, in both `--all` and verbose modes.
- The book labels are checked in `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (Recorded true, Recorded false, Missing) and `index_and_detail_pages_show_each_example_evidence_state` (adds Recorded FIXME). `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` also checks Recorded FIXME on the detail page. The wording of those labels belongs to the cited `requirements.index.state`, so it is not reassessed here.

**Callers select different definitions**
- `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_and_info_accept_a_definition_selection]` shows `status requirements.c*` selects only the matching rows. It includes `requirements.case` and excludes `requirements.ready`.
- The book index lists all definitions, as `index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages` shows.

**Kind-labeled name cells**
- The book index rows are asserted in `index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages` and `index_and_detail_pages_show_each_example_evidence_state`. They have the form ``[`rules.x`](requirements-index/rules.x.html) (example)`` or `(requirement)`.
- The CLI rows are asserted as ``| `requirements.case` (example)`` in `status_and_info_accept_a_definition_selection`.

I found no obligation that lacks a test, and all the tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject.

their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables. The renderer calculates column
widths and aligns the columns. Each caller supplies its state labels:
`habeas status` reports checked evidence states, while the book reports
recorded assessments under {cite}`requirements.index.state`. The CLI keeps
its checked labels: Valid, Missing, Determination false, FIXME, and Invalid.
Callers may select different definitions and supply kind-labeled name cells
so mdBook can link to detail pages.
The requirements index and its detail pages describe the last recorded
assessment as Recorded true, Recorded false, or Recorded FIXME. A missing
record is shown as Missing; an unreadable record or determination is shown as
Unreadable with a readable explanation. Recorded FIXME includes its recorded
These labels describe stored results, without claiming that the record is
current or that repository validation passes. `habeas status` and
`habeas author` check the annotations and evidence.
